notes:
Need searches first.I couldn't write any notes on Amos 6. The research tool hit its usage limit before I could read a single source page, so I have nothing to report.

Here's what happened:
- **First attempt:** I tried to open the commentary pages directly (Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Bible Hub and the NET Bible notes). The tool refused each one, because a page has to come up in a search before it can be opened.
- **Second attempt:** I ran the searches, but the tool ran out of uses at that point. I never saw any results or opened any pages.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any verse notes, tradition comparisons or "other views" sections. Anything I wrote now would be unsourced.

When you start a new turn, I can begin again. I'd search first and then read:
- verse-by-verse commentaries on Enduring Word, Bible Hub (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Barnes), StudyLight and Precept Austin
- the NET Bible notes, which are especially useful for vv. 10 and 12–13 (the text is hard there, and Lo-debar and Karnaim are wordplays)
- Wesley's Notes, Calvin on CCEL and Spurgeon.org, for the different Protestant traditions
- New Advent, Catholic.com and OCA.org, for Catholic and Orthodox readings
- Got Questions and similar sites, for whether vv. 4–6 come up in debates about prosperity teaching

You could also send me the page addresses yourself, and I'd go straight to reading them.
